examples.ko: 이 상자는 모서리가 각져서 손이 아파요.
examples.en: This box has sharp corners and hurts my hand.
He has a face with a square jaw.
Angular stones are dangerous to throw.
I made it round, but one side came out angular.
A cup without sharp edges is comfortable in the hand.
I folded the paper at sharp angles and made a box.

explain: '각지다'는 둥글지 않고 모서리가 반듯하거나 뾰족한 모양이에요. '각진 얼굴, 턱, 어깨'처럼 사람의 모습에 많이 쓰고, 반대는 '둥글다'예요. '각진 어깨'는 어깨선이 곧고 넓어 보이는 느낌이에요.

phrases.en: The angular-shaped plate is pretty.
phrases.nuance_ko: 뒤의 명사를 꾸밀 때 '각진'으로 활용해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use the form 각진 to describe a noun after it.

phrases.en: This bag has angular corners.
phrases.nuance_ko: 문장 끝에서 쓰는 해요체 활용이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The polite form used at the end of a sentence.

phrases.example: 이 의자는 모서리가 각지지 않아서 안전해요.
phrases.en: This chair's corners aren't sharp, so it's safe.
phrases.nuance_ko: 둥글고 부드러운 모양을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to describe a round, soft shape.

explain_en: '각지다' describes a shape with straight or sharp corners rather than a round one. It is common for people's looks, as in '각진 얼굴', '각진 턱' and '각진 어깨'. Its opposite is '둥글다'. A '각진 어깨' means a straight, broad shoulder line.

examples.en: I got rained on and look like a total wreck.
After working all night, I came home looking a mess.
Where are you going looking like that?

examples.ko: 머리도 안 빗고 거지꼴 그대로 나왔어요.
examples.en: He came out looking a mess, without even combing his hair.
After the hike, everyone looked like a mess.
Even though he looked shabby, his expression was bright.

explain: 옷이나 모습이 너무 지저분하고 초라할 때 편하게 쓰는 말이에요. 보통 '거지꼴이 되다', '거지꼴로 다니다'처럼 써요. 남에게 직접 말하면 무례하니 자기 모습이나 친한 사이에서만 쓰세요.

phrases.en: I worked all night, so I look a total mess.
phrases.nuance_ko: '거지꼴'보다 덜 거칠게, 모습이 아주 엉망일 때 쓰는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A milder way than '거지꼴' to say someone looks like a complete mess.

phrases.en: It's fine to walk around looking shabby at home.
phrases.nuance_ko: '거지꼴'을 쓰는 가장 흔한 짝말이고, 자기 모습이나 친한 사이에서 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most common collocation with '거지꼴'; use it about yourself or with close friends.

phrases.example: 시험 때문에 며칠째 거지꼴을 하고 있어요.
phrases.en: I've been looking miserable for days because of exams.
phrases.nuance_ko: '거지꼴이 되다'는 변화를, '거지꼴을 하다'는 그런 모습을 하고 있는 상태를 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: '거지꼴이 되다' describes becoming shabby; '거지꼴을 하다' describes being in that state.

explain_en: It is a casual word for looking very untidy and shabby, typically in '거지꼴이 되다' or '거지꼴로 다니다'. It is rude to say directly to someone, so use it about yourself or with close friends.

en: to be beautiful; to be pretty; to be lovely

examples.en: The bride in a hanbok is really lovely.
The child's hands are so delicate that I hesitate even to touch them.

examples.ko: 곱디고운 목소리로 할머니가 노래를 불러 주셨어요.
examples.en: Grandmother sang for us in a sweet, lovely voice.
The autumn maple leaves have turned a beautiful color.

examples.ko: 세월이 흘러 곱디곱던 얼굴에도 주름이 생겼어요.
examples.en: As time passed, wrinkles appeared even on her once lovely face.

examples.ko: 곱디고울 때 사진을 많이 찍어 두세요.
examples.en: Take lots of photos while she is at her prettiest.

explain: '곱다'를 강하게 말한 표현으로, '높디높다', '크디크다'처럼 형용사를 반복해서 강조하는 꼴이에요. 얼굴, 색, 마음씨, 손에 쓰고 글이나 노랫말에서 자주 보여요. 'ㅂ' 불규칙이라 '곱디고와요', '곱디고운'으로 바뀌어요.

phrases.en: My grandmother has a lovely, kind heart.
phrases.nuance_ko: 겉모습뿐 아니라 마음씨에도 쓸 수 있고 글에서 자주 보여요.
phrases.nuance_en: It can describe a kind heart as well as looks, and often appears in writing.

phrases.en: The color of the hanbok is so beautiful.
phrases.nuance_ko: 해요체로 말할 때 'ㅂ'이 '와'로 바뀌어 '곱디고와요'가 돼요.
phrases.nuance_en: In polite speech the ㅂ changes, giving 곱디고와요.

phrases.en: The baby's face is so lovely.
phrases.nuance_ko: '곱디곱다'의 기본형으로, 강조하지 않고 평범하게 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The basic form of 곱디곱다, used without emphasis.

explain_en: It is an intensified form of '곱다', repeating the adjective just like '높디높다' and '크디크다'. It is used for faces, colors, hearts and hands, and often seen in writing and lyrics. It is a 'ㅂ' irregular adjective: '곱디고와요', '곱디고운'.

examples.en: That actor has a deep, thick voice, which is impressive.
The wooden pillar looks thick and sturdy.
Big, thick raindrops started to fall.
Please write the letters in bold, thick strokes.
These potatoes are really big and thick.

examples.ko: 그 형은 어릴 때부터 팔뚝이 굵직했어요.
examples.en: That older guy has had thick forearms since he was little.

explain: '굵다'보다 꽤 굵고 듬직한 느낌이에요. 목소리나 선, 나무에 쓰고, '굵직한 사건'처럼 크고 중요한 일을 말할 때도 써요.

phrases.en: I wrote my name in thick letters.
phrases.nuance_ko: 글씨나 선이 굵고 눈에 잘 띌 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for thick, easy-to-see lettering or lines.

phrases.en: There were many major events this year.
phrases.nuance_ko: 크고 중요한 일을 말하는 비유적인 쓰임이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A figurative use for big, important events.

phrases.en: I drew a thick line with a pen.
phrases.nuance_ko: 부사로 쓰면 어떻게 그리거나 쓰는지 말할 수 있어요.
phrases.nuance_en: As an adverb it tells how something is drawn or written.

explain_en: Compared with '굵다', it feels solidly thick and dependable. It's used for voices, lines and trees, and also for big, important matters, as in '굵직한 사건'.

examples.ko: 우리 아기는 낯가림이 심해서 처음 보는 사람 품에 안 가요.
examples.en: My baby is shy with strangers and won't go into a new person's arms.

examples.ko: 저는 낯가림이 있어서 새 모임이 어색해요.
examples.en: I'm shy around new people, so new gatherings feel awkward.

examples.ko: 낯가림 때문에 처음에는 말도 못 했어요.
examples.en: Because I'm shy with strangers, I couldn't even speak at first.

examples.ko: 동생은 낯가림이 없어서 누구하고나 잘 놀아요.
examples.en: My younger sibling isn't shy and plays well with anyone.
As my shyness with strangers lessened, I made more friends.
They say a child's stranger shyness is part of growing up.

explain: 동사 '낯을 가리다'의 명사형으로 '낯가림이 심하다/없다'처럼 써요. 아기의 낯가림과 어른의 성격을 말할 때 둘 다 써요.

phrases.en: My daughter is very shy with strangers.
phrases.nuance_ko: 정도가 크다고 말할 때 가장 자주 쓰는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most common collocation for a strong degree.

phrases.en: The baby is shy of strangers, so it cries.
phrases.nuance_ko: 명사 '낯가림'의 원래 동사 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The original verb phrase behind the noun '낯가림'.

phrases.example: 그 아이는 낯가림이 없어서 누구와도 잘 놀아요.
phrases.en: That child isn't shy with strangers, so he plays well with anyone.
phrases.nuance_ko: 반대로 사람을 쉽게 만나는 성격을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The opposite: describes someone who meets people easily.

explain_en: It is the noun form of the verb '낯을 가리다' and is used as '낯가림이 심하다/없다'. It describes both a baby's stranger anxiety and an adult's personality.

examples.en: This product only comes in a single color.

examples.ko: 모든 학생을 단일한 기준으로 평가하기는 어려워요.
examples.en: It is hard to judge every student by a single standard.
The menu is just one item, so choosing is easy.
This shop sells only a single menu item.
The once-unified market split into several.
The company manages all its branches in a unified way.

explain: '하나'만 있다는 뜻인데 일상에서는 '한 가지'나 '하나뿐인'이라고 말해요. '단일'은 '단일 메뉴', '단일 팀'처럼 명사 앞에 붙는 쓰임이 많아요. 반대 느낌의 말은 '다양하다'예요.

phrases.en: This restaurant sells only a single menu item.
phrases.nuance_ko: '단일'을 명사 앞에 붙여 '하나뿐인'이라는 뜻을 나타내요.
phrases.nuance_en: '단일' placed before a noun means 'only one'.

phrases.en: This problem has only one answer.
phrases.nuance_ko: 일상에서는 '단일하다' 대신 이렇게 말하는 경우가 많아요.
phrases.nuance_en: In daily speech, people often say this instead of '단일하다'.

phrases.example: 우리 반 학생들의 생각은 단일하지 않아요.
phrases.en: The students in our class don't all think the same way.
phrases.nuance_ko: 표제어의 부정형으로, 여러 가지가 섞여 있다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The negative form, meaning there is a mix of several kinds.

explain_en: It means there is only one, but in daily speech people say 한 가지 or 하나뿐인. 단일 often attaches before a noun, as in '단일 메뉴' or '단일 팀'. The opposite idea is 다양하다.

examples.ko: 제 피부는 민감성이라 화장품을 고를 때 조심해요.
examples.en: I have sensitive skin, so I'm careful when choosing cosmetics.

examples.ko: 민감성 피부에 맞는 크림을 추천해 주세요.
examples.en: Please recommend a cream that suits sensitive skin.

examples.ko: 아이가 먼지에 대한 민감성이 높아서 자주 재채기를 해요.
examples.en: My child is highly sensitive to dust, so he sneezes often.

examples.ko: 의사가 소리에 대한 민감성을 검사해 봤어요.
examples.en: The doctor tested my sensitivity to sound.

examples.ko: 민감성 치약으로 바꿨더니 이가 덜 시려요.
examples.en: After I switched to toothpaste for sensitive teeth, my teeth hurt less from the cold.
Skin sensitivity gets worse during the change of seasons.

explain: '민감성 피부'처럼 화장품, 피부, 치약 이야기에서 가장 많이 만나요. 성격을 말할 때는 '민감하다', 상태를 설명할 때는 '민감성'을 써요. 반대로 둔한 정도는 '둔감하다'라고 해요.

phrases.en: I have sensitive skin, so I use a mild soap.
phrases.nuance_ko: 가장 흔한 짝말이에요. 피부가 자극에 약하다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most common pairing; it means skin that reacts easily to irritation.

phrases.en: My teeth are sensitive, so I bought sensitive-teeth toothpaste.
phrases.nuance_ko: 제품 이름이나 설명에서 자주 보여요.
phrases.nuance_en: Often seen in product names and descriptions.

phrases.example: 저는 민감성이라서 향이 강한 제품은 못 써요.
phrases.en: I have sensitive skin, so I can't use strongly scented products.
phrases.nuance_ko: 이유를 말할 때 '-라서'를 붙여요. '피부'를 빼도 문맥으로 알 수 있어요.
phrases.nuance_en: Add '-라서' to give a reason. '피부' can be dropped when the context is clear.

explain_en: You meet it most in phrases like '민감성 피부' (sensitive skin) in talk about cosmetics, skin and toothpaste. Use the adjective '민감하다' to describe a person, and '민감성' to name the condition or trait. The opposite adjective is '둔감하다'.

examples.ko: 이 영화는 사랑이라는 보편성을 담고 있어요.
examples.en: This film holds the universality of love.

examples.ko: 음악의 보편성 덕분에 말이 통하지 않아도 즐길 수 있어요.
examples.en: Thanks to the universality of music, you can enjoy it without a shared language.
The importance of family has a universal quality.
Many countries recognize the universality of human rights.

examples.ko: 보편성과 특수성을 함께 생각해 봐야 해요.
examples.en: We need to think about universality and particularity together.

examples.ko: 이 이론은 보편성이 부족하다는 비판을 받아요.
examples.en: This theory is criticized for lacking universality.

explain: 반대말은 '특수성'이고, 둘을 짝으로 자주 말해요. 수업, 발표, 글에서 쓰는 말이라 일상 대화에서는 '누구에게나 해당되는 점'처럼 풀어서 말하기도 해요. 형용사처럼 쓰면 '보편적이다'가 돼요.

phrases.en: Let's look at both the universality and the particularity of culture.
phrases.nuance_ko: 반대말 '특수성'과 짝으로 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Often paired with its opposite, '특수성' (particularity).

phrases.example: 이 이야기는 보편성이 있어서 누구나 공감해요.
phrases.en: This story has universality, so everyone can relate to it.
phrases.nuance_ko: 어떤 것이 누구에게나 해당된다고 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to say that something applies to everyone.

phrases.en: Love is a universal emotion that everyone feels.
phrases.nuance_ko: '보편성'을 형용사처럼 쓴 모양이에요. 명사를 꾸밀 때 편해요.
phrases.nuance_en: The adjective form of '보편성', handy for modifying nouns.

explain_en: Its opposite is '특수성' (particularity), and the two are often paired. It belongs to classes, presentations and writing, so in daily talk people might say 'something that applies to everyone'. The adjective-like form is '보편적이다'.

examples.en: We learned how to find the area of a sector in math class.
A slice of pizza is shaped like a fan.
I folded paper and made a fan shape.
The problem of finding the central angle of a sector was hard.
The peacock spread its tail wide like a fan.

examples.ko: 이 공원의 무대는 부채꼴로 되어 있어요.
examples.en: The stage in this park is fan-shaped.

explain: 수학에서는 원의 일부인 도형을 가리키지만, 일상에서는 한쪽이 좁고 점점 넓어지는 모양을 비유로도 말해요. '부채 모양'이라고도 해요. '-꼴'은 모양을 나타내요.

phrases.en: I folded the paper into a fan shape.
phrases.nuance_ko: '부채꼴'과 같은 뜻으로 일상에서 편하게 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Same idea as 부채꼴, used casually in daily life.

phrases.en: I cut the pizza into wedge shapes.
phrases.nuance_ko: 조각의 모양을 말할 때 '-로'를 붙여서 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Add 로 to describe the shape something is cut into.

phrases.en: The fireworks spread out in a fan shape.
phrases.nuance_ko: 한 점에서 점점 넓게 퍼지는 모습에 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Describes something spreading wider from a single point.
phrases.en_equiv: to spread in a fan shape

explain_en: In math it names a shape that is part of a circle (a sector), but in daily life it also describes any shape that starts narrow and widens out. You can also say '부채 모양'. The '-꼴' part means 'shape'.

examples.en: I bought a triangular rice ball at the convenience store.

examples.ko: 삼각 모양의 지붕이 멀리서도 눈에 띄어요.
examples.en: The triangle-shaped roof stands out even from far away.

examples.ko: 드라마 속 삼각관계 때문에 사람들이 싸웠어요.
examples.en: People argued because of the love triangle in the drama.

examples.ko: 사진 찍을 때 삼각대를 꼭 챙겨 가요.
examples.en: When I take photos, I always bring a tripod.
In math class, I drew lines with a set square.

examples.ko: 삼각형의 세 변을 더하면 둘레를 구할 수 있어요.
examples.en: If you add up the three sides of a triangle, you get its perimeter.

explain: 삼각은 혼자 쓰기보다 삼각형, 삼각김밥, 삼각관계, 삼각대처럼 다른 말과 붙여서 써요. '삼각형'은 도형 이름이고, '세모'는 어린이와 일상 대화에서 더 자주 써요.

phrases.en: I drew a triangle in my notebook.
phrases.nuance_ko: 도형 이름으로 쓰는 가장 기본적인 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most basic word for the shape.

phrases.en: I bought a triangle-shaped snack.
phrases.nuance_ko: 어린이와 일상 대화에서 더 자주 쓰는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: More common with children and in everyday talk.

phrases.en: I set up a tripod to take a photo.
phrases.nuance_ko: 카메라를 세우는 세 발 달린 도구를 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: A three-legged stand for holding a camera.

explain_en: 삼각 is rarely used alone; it joins other words like 삼각형, 삼각김밥, 삼각관계, and 삼각대. 삼각형 is the formal shape name, while 세모 is more common with children and in daily talk.

en: to be trivial; to be trifling; to be small

examples.en: I keep small moments of daily life in photos.
On payday I bought a small gift.
Happiness is small, so it lasts longer.
We decided to hold the gathering in a modest way.

examples.ko: 소소한 문제는 제가 먼저 해결해 볼게요.
examples.en: I'll try to solve the minor problems first.
This task looks minor, but it is important.

explain: 소소하다는 작고 대단하지 않지만 마음이 편하고 따뜻한 느낌으로 요즘 많이 써요. '소소한 행복'이 대표적이에요. 크기만 작을 때는 '작다'를 쓰고, 소소하다는 일이나 즐거움에 어울려요.

phrases.example: 저는 퇴근 후 커피 한 잔의 소소한 행복을 즐겨요.
phrases.en: After work I enjoy the little happiness of a cup of coffee.
phrases.nuance_ko: 크지 않지만 일상에서 느끼는 작은 즐거움을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: A small joy felt in everyday life, not a big event.

explain_en: 소소하다 means small and unremarkable, often with a warm, comfortable feeling, and is popular now. '소소한 행복' (small happiness) is the typical phrase. For plain size use 작다; 소소하다 fits tasks and pleasures.

en: to be dainty; to be lovely

examples.ko: 아기가 신은 작은 신발이 너무 앙증맞아요.
examples.en: The tiny shoes the baby is wearing are so adorable.
I received a cute little puppy doll as a gift.
The cat waves its front paw in an adorable way.
It's a cute little cup, so the kids like it.

examples.ko: 친구들은 제 작은 가방이 앙증맞다고 했어요.
examples.en: My friends said my little bag was dainty and cute.
It's a key chain so cute that my eyes keep going to it.

explain: '귀엽다'보다 좁아서 작고 아기자기하게 귀여운 물건이나 동물, 아기에게 써요. 큰 물건에는 잘 안 맞아요. 비슷한 말로 '깜찍하다', '아기자기하다'가 있어요.

phrases.en: I bought a cup that looks dainty and cute.
phrases.nuance_ko: 생김새를 설명할 때 쓰는 활용이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to describe how something looks.

phrases.en: This key chain is really cute and adorable.
phrases.nuance_ko: 작고 귀여운 느낌이 비슷하지만, '깜찍하다'가 조금 더 귀엽고 재치 있어요.
phrases.nuance_en: Similar small-and-cute feel, but a bit more charming and clever.

phrases.en: The cafe is cute and cozy, so it's great for taking photos.
phrases.nuance_ko: 작은 것들이 예쁘게 모여 있을 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when small things are arranged charmingly together.

explain_en: It is narrower than '귀엽다' and is used for small, neat and cute things, animals and babies. It doesn't suit big objects well. Similar words include '깜찍하다' and '아기자기하다'.

examples.ko: 올록볼록한 포장지를 만지면 재미있는 소리가 나요.
examples.en: When you touch the bumpy wrapping paper, it makes a fun sound.
My skin came up in bumps, so I went to the hospital.

examples.ko: 올록볼록 무늬가 있는 컵이라 손에 잘 잡혀요.
examples.en: The cup has a bumpy pattern, so it's easy to hold.
The wall was uneven, so I repainted it.
I pressed a bumpy pattern onto the cookies.

examples.ko: 얼음이 올록볼록 얼어서 스케이트를 타기 힘들어요.
examples.en: The ice froze unevenly, so it's hard to skate.

explain: 표면이 고르지 않고 작게 튀어나오고 들어간 모습이에요. '울퉁불퉁'과 비슷하지만 '올록볼록'은 작은 것이 둥글게 튀어나온 느낌이 있어요.

phrases.en: The surface of this wall is bumpy.
phrases.nuance_ko: '하다'를 붙여 상태를 말하는 형용사가 돼요.
phrases.nuance_en: Adding 하다 makes it an adjective describing a state.

phrases.en: I made cookies with a bumpy pattern.
phrases.nuance_ko: 명사 앞에서 꾸밀 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used before a noun to describe it.

phrases.en: The road is uneven, so it's hard to walk.
phrases.nuance_ko: '올록볼록'보다 크고 거친 느낌이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Feels bigger and rougher than 올록볼록.

explain_en: It describes a surface that is not flat, with small parts sticking out and sinking in. It is similar to '울퉁불퉁', but '올록볼록' has a feel of small, rounded bumps.

examples.ko: 외관상 이 건물은 아주 튼튼해 보여요.
examples.en: From the outside, this building looks very sturdy.

examples.ko: 이 중고 차는 외관상으로는 새것이나 다름없어요.
examples.en: This used car looks just like a new one from the outside.

examples.ko: 외관상 흠집은 없지만 작동이 안 돼요.
examples.en: There are no scratches on the outside, but it doesn't work.

examples.ko: 이 집은 외관상 예쁜데 살기에는 불편해요.
examples.en: This house looks pretty, but it's inconvenient to live in.

examples.ko: 외관상 두 가구는 거의 같아 보여요.
examples.en: In appearance, the two pieces of furniture look almost the same.

examples.ko: 외관상의 차이는 작아도 가격은 두 배예요.
examples.en: The difference in looks is small, but the price is double.

explain: 건물, 물건, 제품의 겉모습을 말할 때 자주 쓰고, '외견상'과 거의 비슷해요. 뒤에 '하지만'이 오면서 겉과 속이 다르다는 말로 이어지는 일이 많아요. 일상 대화에서는 '겉보기에'라고도 해요.

phrases.en: On the outside, this house looks very clean.
phrases.nuance_ko: '으로는'을 붙이면 겉으로 볼 때만 그렇다는 뜻이 분명해져요.
phrases.nuance_en: Adding 'euroneun' makes it clear this holds only from the outside.

phrases.example: 외관상 문제는 없지만 안은 아직 몰라요.
phrases.en: There's no problem on the outside, but I don't know about the inside yet.
phrases.nuance_ko: 겉모습에 보이는 문제를 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for a problem that can be seen on the outside.

phrases.en: By its look, this watch seems new.
phrases.nuance_ko: 뜻이 같고, 일상 대화에서 더 편하게 쓰는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Same meaning, and more casual for daily speech.

explain_en: It is often used for the outer look of buildings, objects and products, and is almost the same as '외견상'. It often leads into a contrast, like 'but the inside is different'. In daily talk people also say '겉보기에'.

en: valor; bravery (shown in battle or danger)

examples.en: The soldiers became widely known for their valor.
The bravery of the tiger often appears in old tales.

examples.ko: 그 장군의 용맹을 칭찬하는 노래가 있어요.
examples.en: There is a song praising that general's valor.

examples.ko: 용맹과 지혜를 함께 갖춘 사람이 되고 싶어요.
examples.en: I want to become a person who has both valor and wisdom.

examples.ko: 그 부대는 전쟁에서 보여 준 용맹 덕분에 훈장을 받았어요.
examples.en: The unit received a medal thanks to the valor it showed in the war.
The children were moved by the firefighter's courage.

explain: '용기'는 일상에서 누구나 쓰는 말이고, 용맹은 전쟁·싸움·위험한 상황에서 보이는 씩씩하고 사나운 힘에 가까워요. 그래서 '용기를 내다'는 말해도 '용맹을 내다'는 안 해요. 군인, 장군, 호랑이 같은 말과 잘 어울려요.

phrases.en: The general displayed great valor in the war.
phrases.nuance_ko: 용맹을 널리 보여 준다는 뜻이고 용맹과 가장 잘 어울리는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means showing valor widely; the best-matching verb for 용맹.

phrases.en: He has both courage and wisdom.
phrases.nuance_ko: 옛이야기 속 영웅을 설명할 때 자주 짝지어 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Often paired when describing heroes in old stories.

phrases.en: His brave appearance is really cool.
phrases.nuance_ko: 용맹의 느낌이 있다는 뜻의 형용사예요.
phrases.nuance_en: An adjective meaning having a sense of valor.

explain_en: '용기' is an everyday word anyone uses, while '용맹' is closer to bold, fierce strength shown in war, fighting or danger. So you say '용기를 내다' but not '용맹을 내다'. It goes well with soldiers, generals and tigers.

examples.en: This is the only bakery in the neighborhood.
My only hobby is photography.

examples.ko: 유일하게 그 사람만 제 말을 믿었어요.
examples.en: He was the only one who believed me.
This method might be the only one.

examples.ko: 그 아이는 우리 집의 유일한 손자예요.
examples.en: That child is our family's only grandson.
It is precious because it is one of a kind.

explain: '유일하다'는 주로 '유일한 + 명사' 모양으로 써요. '하나뿐인'이라고 말하는 일상 표현보다 조금 딱딱하게 들려요. '유일하게'는 부사처럼 '그 사람만'이라는 느낌을 줘요.

phrases.example: 이게 문제를 풀 수 있는 유일한 방법이에요.
phrases.en: This is the only way to solve the problem.
phrases.nuance_ko: 다른 것은 없고 하나뿐이라는 뜻으로 가장 자주 쓰는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most common pairing, meaning there is no other option.

phrases.en: Only one person got the right answer.
phrases.nuance_ko: '그 사람만'이라는 느낌을 주는 부사로 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used as an adverb with the feeling of 'only that person'.

phrases.en: This book is the only one in the world.
phrases.nuance_ko: '유일하다'보다 부드러운 일상 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A softer, everyday way to say 유일하다.

explain_en: It mostly appears as a modifier before a noun. It sounds a little more formal than everyday words for 'the only one'. The adverb form carries the feeling of 'only that person'.

examples.ko: 이 동네는 인정미가 넘쳐서 살기 좋아요.
examples.en: This neighborhood overflows with warmth, so it's a good place to live.
I felt the warmth of the market vendors.
There are many warm-hearted neighbors, so I feel reassured.
I could feel kindness from the restaurant owner.
It's hard to find warmth in cities these days.

examples.ko: 인정미 넘치는 사람들과 함께 일하고 싶어요.
examples.en: I want to work with people full of warmth.

explain: 사람들 사이의 따뜻한 정이 느껴지는 분위기를 말해요. 일상에서는 그냥 '정'이라고 많이 하고, '인정미'는 '인정미가 넘치다/있다'처럼 조금 글 같은 말투로 써요.

phrases.example: 이 시장은 인정미가 넘쳐서 자주 와요.
phrases.en: This market is full of warmth, so I come often.
phrases.nuance_ko: 따뜻한 분위기를 칭찬할 때 쓰는 대표적인 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A typical phrase for praising a warm atmosphere.

phrases.en: I felt the kindness of people at a small shop.
phrases.nuance_ko: 사람들의 정을 직접 경험했다고 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when you have personally experienced people's warmth.

phrases.en: People in the countryside are full of warmth.
phrases.nuance_ko: '인정미'보다 일상에서 훨씬 자주 쓰는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Much more common in daily speech than 인정미.

explain_en: It describes an atmosphere where warm feeling between people can be felt. In everyday speech people often just say '정', while '인정미' is a bit more written, as in '인정미가 넘치다/있다'.

examples.en: Looking at a 3D picture, it feels real.
If you think in a multi-dimensional way, the problem gets easier.
A pop-up card came as a gift.
It is a photo with a strong sense of depth.
This building is known for its three-dimensional design.
That novel is fun because the characters have depth.

explain: '평면'의 반대말이에요. 눈에 보이는 물건뿐 아니라 '입체적인 인물'처럼 여러 면이 있는 사람이나 설명을 칭찬할 때도 써요. 영상이나 게임에서는 '3D'라는 말이 더 많이 들려요.

phrases.en: The characters in this novel are very well-rounded.
phrases.nuance_ko: 여러 면이 있어 깊이가 느껴질 때 칭찬으로 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: A compliment for something with many sides and depth.

phrases.en: I made a 3D shape out of paper.
phrases.nuance_ko: 수학 시간에 자주 나오는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A common phrase in math class.

phrases.en: It looks more vivid in 3D video.
phrases.nuance_ko: 영상에서는 '3D'라고도 많이 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: For video, people also often just say '3D'.

explain_en: The opposite of '평면' (flat). Besides visible objects, it praises people or explanations that have many sides, as in '입체적인 인물'. In videos and games, you hear '3D' more often.

examples.en: This mirror is oval, so it looks pretty.
An egg is close to an oval shape.
I put the salad on an oval plate.
Planets travel along elliptical orbits.
Glasses suit me because my face is oval.

examples.ko: 타원형 테이블은 방에 들어가기엔 너무 커요.
examples.en: The oval table is too big to fit in the room.

explain: 동그란 '원형'을 옆으로 길게 늘인 모양을 말해요. 달걀 모양은 '계란형'이라고도 하는데, 얼굴이나 모양을 말할 때 많이 써요. '타원'만 쓰기도 하지만 모양을 말할 때는 '타원형'이 자연스러워요.

phrases.en: I put the fish dish on an oval plate.
phrases.nuance_ko: 물건 이름 앞에 붙여서 그 모양을 설명해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Placed before an object's name to describe its shape.

phrases.en: Our dining table is oval.
phrases.nuance_ko: 모양을 설명하는 가장 기본적인 문장이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most basic sentence pattern for describing a shape.

phrases.en: The track on the field is close to an ellipse.
phrases.nuance_ko: '타원형'보다 짧고, 모양 자체를 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Shorter than '타원형'; names the shape itself.

explain_en: This is a shape like a round circle (원형) stretched lengthwise. An egg-like shape is also called '계란형', often for faces. You can say just '타원', but '타원형' sounds natural when describing a shape.

examples.ko: 시골 할머니 댁에서 키운 토종 닭을 먹었어요.
examples.en: I ate a native chicken raised at my grandmother's house in the countryside.

examples.ko: 이 나무는 외국에서 온 게 아니라 토종이에요.
examples.en: This tree didn't come from abroad; it's native.

examples.ko: 토종 꿀은 수입 꿀보다 값이 비싸요.
examples.en: Native honey is more expensive than imported honey.

examples.ko: 요즘은 토종 씨앗을 지키는 사람들이 늘고 있어요.
examples.en: These days, more people are protecting native seeds.

examples.ko: 저는 토종 한국인이라서 김치 없으면 힘들어요.
examples.en: I'm a Korean through and through, so it's hard without kimchi.

examples.ko: 토종 브랜드가 해외에서도 인기를 얻고 있어요.
examples.en: A homegrown brand is gaining popularity overseas too.

explain: 그 땅에서 오래 살아온 동물이나 식물에 써요. 반대로 외국에서 들어온 것은 '외래종'이라고 해요. 사람에게 쓰면 '토종 한국인'처럼 입맛이나 생활이 아주 한국적이라는 농담 같은 느낌이 돼요.

phrases.en: Native Korean chicken is chewier than regular chicken.
phrases.nuance_ko: 한국에서 오래 키워 온 닭이에요. '토종'이 붙는 가장 흔한 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Chicken long raised in Korea; one of the most common words with 토종.

phrases.en: This fish is not native; it's an introduced species.
phrases.nuance_ko: '토종'의 반대말이에요. 외국에서 들어온 동물이나 식물을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: The opposite of 토종: animals or plants brought in from abroad.

phrases.example: 저는 토종 한국인이라 김치가 꼭 있어야 해요.
phrases.en: I'm a true Korean, so I must have kimchi.
phrases.nuance_ko: 사람에게 쓰면 입맛이나 생활이 아주 한국적이라는 농담 같은 느낌이 있어요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used jokingly for a person whose tastes or habits are very Korean.

explain_en: It is used for animals and plants that have lived in a place for a long time. The opposite, something that came from abroad, is '외래종'. Said about a person, as in '토종 한국인', it has a joking feel of being very Korean in taste and lifestyle.
